items.headline: California Legislature Passes AB 2047 Mandating Firearm-Blocking Technology for 3D Printers
items.summary: The California Legislature passed Assembly Bill 2047, sending the Firearm Printing Prevention Act to Governor Newsom for signature. The measure requires consumer 3D printers sold or transferred in California to incorporate DOJ-compliant firearm-blocking technology and software algorithms to prevent unauthorized manufacturing of firearms and conversion devices. State regulators are tasked with establishing official performance standards and certification guidelines prior to full enforcement.
items.community_takeaway: California firearm owners and 3D printing enthusiasts should monitor state DOJ regulatory releases regarding hardware certification standards and compliance timelines.

items.headline: Ninth Circuit Rehears Baird v. Bonta En Banc, Staying Challenge to Urban Open-Carry Ban
items.statute_or_case: Baird v. Bonta (9th Cir. No. 24-565 / CA Penal Code § 26350)
items.summary: The full Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals granted en banc review in Baird v. Bonta, vacating a prior three-judge panel decision that had briefly declared California's urban open-carry ban unconstitutional. The full court heard oral arguments in June 2026 while keeping the state's public open-carry prohibitions fully in place pending final disposition. The decision leaves urban open-carry restrictions active in counties with populations exceeding 200,000.
items.community_takeaway: California firearm owners must continue adhering to statutory open-carry prohibitions in populous counties while the Ninth Circuit completes en banc deliberation.
items.source_name: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit

items.headline: CA DOJ Issues Updated CCW Fingerprint Guidance and Driver's License Scanner Advisory
items.statute_or_case: CA DOJ Information Bulletin 2026-DLE-13 & Advisory No. 183
items.summary: The California Department of Justice Bureau of Firearms released Information Bulletin 2026-DLE-13, clarifying non-resident CCW applicant fingerprinting protocols using federal FD-258 cards pursuant to court injunctions. Additionally, the DOJ issued Advisory No. 183 instructing firearm dealers on barcode scanning requirements for redesigned state driver's licenses. These directives aim to standardize eligibility verification across local licensing authorities and retail vendors.
items.community_takeaway: Non-resident applicants and licensed dealers should review updated DOJ bulletins to ensure local agency compliance with federal submission standards and retail scanner compatibility.
items.source_name: California Department of Justice Bureau of Firearms

items.headline: Ninth Circuit Dismisses California Lawsuit Seeking Stricter Federal Ghost Gun Rules
items.statute_or_case: State of California v. ATF (9th Circuit Court of Appeals)
items.summary: Reuters reported that the Ninth U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals threw out a challenge brought by California Attorney General Rob Bonta and gun safety advocates against federal ATF ghost gun regulations. A unanimous three-judge panel found that California failed to show the legal standing or concrete injury required to challenge federal receiver rules. The decision preserves current federal ATF component guidelines across state lines.
items.community_takeaway: While federal ATF rules remain intact nationally, California residents and firearm retailers remain subject to stringent state-level ghost gun, serialization, and background check laws.

items.headline: CalMatters Investigation Details Ongoing Enforcement Challenges in State Prohibited Persons Database
items.statute_or_case: Armed and Prohibited Persons System (APPS) / CalMatters Reporting
items.summary: An investigative report by CalMatters analyzed structural hurdles in California's Armed and Prohibited Persons System (APPS), which tracks registered gun owners who become disqualified due to criminal convictions or court orders. The report highlighted a backlog exceeding 24,000 individuals alongside staffing constraints in state enforcement units. Local law enforcement agencies and judicial officers cite data-syncing gaps as a primary cause of enforcement delay.
items.community_takeaway: Individuals facing disqualifying court orders or protective restrictions must follow legal relinquishment pathways promptly through licensed dealers or local law enforcement to ensure public safety and compliance.

items.headline: California Retail Firearm & Ammunition 11% Excise Tax
items.summary: California's Gun Violence Prevention and School Safety Act levies an 11% state excise tax on gross receipts from retail sales of firearms, precursor parts, and ammunition.
items.community_takeaway: First-time buyers should account for the 11% surcharge added at checkout alongside standard local sales taxes when budgeting for ammunition and home storage hardware.
items.source_name: California Department of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA)

items.headline: Status of California's '1-in-30 Day' Firearm Purchase Restriction
items.statute_or_case: Nguyen v. Bonta / CA Penal Code § 27535
items.summary: Legal challenges against California's prohibition on purchasing more than one handgun or centerfire rifle within a 30-day period continue through appellate review following district court injunctions and administrative stays.
items.community_takeaway: Dealers across California continue to enforce the 30-day waiting window on purchase submissions. Always confirm your last DROS release date with your local FFL dealer before initiating a new application.
items.source_name: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit

items.headline: Strict Criminal Storage Enforcement & Lockbox Distribution
items.summary: State law enforcement agencies have issued reminders emphasizing strict felony liability for criminal storage where unauthorized minors or prohibited individuals gain access to unattended firearms.
items.community_takeaway: Storing a firearm under a mattress or in a nightstand drawer is not legal compliance. Firearms must be secured with a California DOJ-certified lock or inside a locked safe container.

items.headline: Vehicle Transport & Mandatory Unloaded Locked Container Standards
items.summary: California requires all handguns transported in a motor vehicle to be completely unloaded and locked inside the trunk or in a fully enclosed locked container. Glove compartments and center consoles are expressly prohibited by statute.
items.community_takeaway: Place firearms inside a locked lockbox in the back of SUVs or hatchbacks, and transport ammunition in a separate compartment or bag.

items.headline: In-Person Ammunition Eligibility Verification Mandates
items.summary: Retail ammunition transfers remain restricted to face-to-face transactions through licensed ammunition vendors with real-time electronic DOJ eligibility checks.
items.community_takeaway: Ensure your California Driver's License matches your address in the Automated Firearms System (AFS) to qualify for the instant $1 background check rather than the $19 manual check.

items.headline: 9th Circuit Review of SB 2 Concealed Carry 'Sensitive Places'
items.statute_or_case: May v. Bonta / SB 2 (CA Penal Code § 26230)
items.summary: Appellate proceedings regarding California's restrictions on lawful concealed carry across public and private commercial properties without express owner signage remain under federal judicial scrutiny.
items.community_takeaway: Permit holders should review local sheriff and police department guidance regarding currently enforceable prohibited zones and private property rules.
items.source_name: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
